LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. The former first-round pick had 11 carries for 36 yards and caught five of his seven targets for 55 yards (and a receiving score) in the loss to Detroit. He has a great matchup against a Carolina defense that is 30th in EPA/Rush, 32nd in yards per carry allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) this season. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. home.headline: Packers get exciting injury update on Micah Parsons: Report
home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers expect superstar pass rusher Micah Parsons to return to practice next week, according to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport on Thursday. “Micah Parsons is expected to return to practice next week. Obviously short week, was not able to do it this week. Next week he should be on the practice field if all goes well. And that is an excellent thing for the Green Bay Packers,” Rapoport said. “I expect caution as far as when he’s actually on the playing field. They want to make sure everything around his knee is as strong as possible. “They are taking their time, but his return is coming.” The Packers will take the field for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Carolina Panthers later this evening. Parsons’ next opportunity to return to the field for in-game action is a Week 9 matchup against the New England Patriots next Sunday. The Packers have been without their generational pass rusher for the entirety of the season thus far, as he continues to recover from the ACL tear he suffered in Week 15 of Green Bay’s 2025 campaign. Green Bay faces off against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 10 before taking their bye in Week 11. Thursday night’s matchup against the Panthers will kick off at 8:15 p.m. ET. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Both of these AFC teams are contenders to win the Super Bowl this season, and the Ravens are expected to get Lamar Jackson back in action after he missed three games with a sprained ankle. The Ravens won just one of the three games that Jackson missed, and their offense has struggled over the last two weeks in losses against AFC North opponents in Cleveland and Cincinnati. The Ravens don't want to fall back to .500 this season, and they're set as small underdogs on the road against Buffalo. With every team in the AFC North sitting at over .500 this season, the Ravens can't afford too many more losses, especially against teams that they may be competing for a wild card spot against. Right now, the Bills are in first place in the AFC East, and they're coming off their bye week after a 5-1 start to the season. Josh Allen is the leading candidate to win the MVP award, and he's been terrific as both a passer and a runner. Now, he takes on a Baltimore defense that features Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey, Nate Wiggins and others in the secondary that could make it tough on a Buffalo passing game that has been short-handed at receiver for a lot of the season. The Bills are hoping to keep things rolling out of their bye, as they're two games up in the loss column on the New England Patriots in the AFC East. Oddsmakers have set Buffalo as a favorite at home, and there are several players on both of these teams that are worth a look in the prop market. So, ahead of this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made player prop picks, game picks, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more to help you wager on Bills vs. Ravens. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Ravens vs. Bills in Week 8 Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Baltimore Ravens +3.5 (-110) vs. Buffalo Bills – Iain MacMillan Josh Allen OVER 7.5 Rush Attempts (+106) – Peter Dewey Zay Flowers Anytime TD (+165) – Peter Dewey Ja’Kobi Lane OVER 2.5 Receptions (-134) – Peter Dewey Each week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . He’s taking the Ravens to cover with Jackson expected back in the lineup: Betting on this game hinges on whether or not Lamar Jackson is going to be able to suit up for the Ravens. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. Allen has been awesome on the ground this season, carrying the ball 48 times (eight times per game) for 240 yards and eight scores. Allen is the preferred option for the Bills in short yardage, handling eight or more carries in three of his six games. Fresh out of a bye, I expect Allen to be as healthy as he’s been this season, which could be a good sign for him using his legs. The Ravens are allowing over four yards per carry to opposing quarterbacks, and Allen had 14 carries in the meeting between these teams during the 2025 regular season. Baltimore ranks 12th in the league in EPA/Rush, so the Bills and Joe Brady may get creative with the running game rather than riding James Cook (who has had fumbling issues) on Sunday. At plus money, this prop is worth a shot for the former league MVP. Ravens star Zay Flowers has been one of the best receivers in the NFL this season, catching 40 of his 53 targets (in six games) for 608 yards and three scores. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. After all, the Bills are dead last in the league in EPA/Play on defense. Buffalo’s pass defense is one of the worst in the league, ranking 29th in EPA/Pass while allowing 15 passing scores. Opposing wide receivers have torched the Bills, scoring 11 touchdowns across six games – the most allowed to the position in the NFL. It doesn’t get much better for Flowers, who is averaging over 100 yards per game and has caught at least five passes in every matchup. Since these teams combined for 81 points the last time they played, I’d expect another up-and-down matchup with a ton of offensive possessions for both sides. Flowers has simply been too effective in space, and he has the fourth-highest target share in the NFL this season. That puts him in a great spot to find the end zone for the second week in a row on Sunday. Ravens rookie Ja’Kobi Lane has played just one game with Lamar Jackson, catching one of his three targets in Week 1 against the Indianapolis Colts for 11 yards. The third-round pick missed time with a wrist injury, but he’s returned to play a major role in this offense the last two weeks. Lane played 54.4 percent of the team’s snaps in Week 6 and 68.7 percent of the snaps in Week 7, receiving five targets in each game. He reeled in seven of those passes for 65 yards. While those aren’t huge numbers, Lane has cleared this prop in back-to-back games, and he saw three targets in limited snaps in the opener before going down. Jackson is an immediate boost to Baltimore’s passing offense, so I think Lane is a great bet to clear this prop for the third game in a row, especially if his snap share continues to rise. The total in this matchup is all the way up at 54.5, and it's worth noting that the last time these teams met in the regular season, they combined for 81 points. There are a ton of awesome playmakers in this game, including Derrick Henry, James Cook, Zay Flowers, Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore and others that could make an impact by scoring a touchdown. So, why don't we bet on a few players to do exactly that? The anytime touchdown scorer market is one of the most exciting ways to bet on the NFL, especially when two of the league's top quarterbacks – Jackson and Josh Allen – are facing off. While Henry, Cook, and Allen are all set at minus odds to find the end zone, I've decided to look at three players at plus money that could score in Week 8. Here's a breakdown of the odds for these picks and my analysis ahead of Sunday’s Raves vs/ Bills clash. Flowers has three games with double-digit targets, and he’s by far the No. 1 option in this passing game. Now, with Jackson expected to return, Flowers should get a major boost against a defense that has not been able to guard anyone in the passing game. Both of these teams are considered Super Bowl contenders in the latest odds at the best betting sites , and they feature two of the best quarterbacks in the league. Lamar Jackson (ankle) has not played since the first half of Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans, but he is expected to return on Sunday in what has suddenly become a huge game for the Ravens. Baltimore is 4-3 this season after going 1-2 in the games Jackson missed, and it’s in last place in the AFC North with every team in the division over .500. The Ravens dropped back-to-back key division games against Cleveland and Cincinnati without the two-time league MVP. Josh Allen – the MVP favorite this season – and the Bills are coming out of their bye week to play in this game, and they’re favored at home after a 5-1 start. Buffalo is looking to get the top spot in the AFC, and it benefitted from a Kansas City Chiefs loss (now 5-1 as well) during Week 7. Sunday’s game is the eighth meeting between Jackson and Allen all-time, with the Ravens holding a 3-2 edge in the regular season while Allen has won both of his playoff matchups against Jackson. Who has the edge in this regular-season clash? All season long, the SI Betting team has been predicting the final score of NFL games, and this one is no different. Using the latest odds and analysis from our team, here’s my score prediction for Sunday’s marquee matchup in Week 8. Ravens vs. Bills Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Ravens +3 (+100) Bills -3 (-120) 54.5 (Over -108/Under -112) The odds for this game are moving in the Ravens’ favor, as Buffalo opened as a 3.5-point favorite with Jackson’s status still up in the air. The star quarterback reportedly is in line to play on Sunday, and he’s now practiced in back-to-back weeks despite dealing with an ankle injury. He certainly gives the Ravens’ offense a higher ceiling than backup Tyler Huntley. Ravens vs. Bills Score Prediction Each week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . He’s taking the Ravens to cover with Jackson expected back in the lineup: Betting on this game hinges on whether or not Lamar Jackson is going to be able to suit up for the Ravens. Unfortunately, I place my bets early in the week, so I don't have the benefit of knowing whether or not the two-time MVP will be on the field on Sunday. The betting line indicates that he will, so I'm going to trust that, along with the reports that Jesse Minter is optimistic that Jackson will be ready to go. When a team only has one loss on their schedule, and they have the best quarterback in football on their roster, a lot of their issues are overlooked. That's the case for the Bills, whose defense has been horrendous this season, ranking 30th in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. They are the only defense in football that ranks in the bottom three in both of those metrics. I hesitate to lay more than a field goal on any team with that bad of a defense, especially when that defense potentially has to face another MVP candidate at quarterback. I'll take the points with Baltimore on Sunday. The last two meetings between Allen and Jackson have been decided by two points (their playoff game in the 2024 season) and one point (their matchup in the 2025 regular season). Buffalo’s defense is last in the NFL in EPA/Play and 30th in success rate, so this could be a get-right game for Jackson and Co. if he’s able to play at his full capabilities. It’s hard to put too much stock into the Ravens last three games without him, though their defense is now 13th in yards per play allowed and 15th in success rate. That’s not terrible, especially since Joe Burrow torched this team in the second half. I expect a high-scoring affair on Sunday, and it wouldn’t shock me if this came down to a final field goal. away.headline: Ravens star under fire for what he said after Lamar Jackson injury vs Bills
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens could be without quarterback Lamar Jackson for the rest of the season after a concerning injury knocked him out of Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills. He was ruled out for the remainder of the game, leaving the Ravens in a difficult situation at quarterback as they suffered a loss to Buffalo. According to postgame reports and comments from Ravens head coach Jesse Minter, Jackson will be placed on injured reserve, undergo surgery, and miss at least four games. “I mean this with no disrespect, but like that [expletive] has nothing to do with us. We’re a defense, and at the end of the day you need to go out there and play how you want to be remembered,” he told reporters. “And you gotta play with a certain passion, which I felt we did. Obviously, not what we want on the scoreboard, but there’s a passion factor when you go out there. Guys look each other in the eyes and play passionate,” Hamilton said. “He thought he was being a tough guy now he’ll send out an apology,” another commenter wrote. Jackson was attempting to pass the ball on his first offensive play of the game, but his throwing hand made contact with Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau. Jackson grabbed his right thumb, then left the field and went back to the locker room. Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton may not have won over some fans when asked about what sort of message he gives to teammates when an injury hits the star quarterback. More news: NFL Insider Floats Ravens QB Trade Target After Lamar Jackson Injury Hamilton’s comments sparked criticism on social media, with several fans taking issue with his response. “Insane not to care about the reason your team wins,” one commenter responded to the X video clip . Someone commented, “Lmao nothing to do with him. He’s the face of the franchise.” “son he is your team hope respectfully we talking about 2 time mvp Lamar Jackson,” a commenter replied. Others wrote in the replies, “locker room crumbling . . .,” and “That’s a terrible answer.” However, other fans defended Hamilton, suggesting he was emphasizing the defense’s responsibility to continue playing hard regardless of injuries on offense. Not only did Jackson leave the game with his right thumb injury, but backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also exited due to a toe injury. Undrafted rookie third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano entered the game to try to lead the Ravens to a surprising win. Baltimore’s defense struggled to contain Buffalo’s offense, which generated 426 total yards behind quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook, and others. Allen threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win, and ran for another. Cook finished with 21 carries for 80 rushing yards and a touchdown. The 4-4 Ravens are in a difficult spot with their quarterbacks now. It was unclear on Sunday night if Huntley would be able to start in their upcoming game. Ravens Turn to Joe Fagnano After Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley Suffer Injuries Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Shawn Hubbard/Baltimore Ravens Photos QB Joe Fagnano The Ravens' quarterback injuries didn't stop with Lamar Jackson. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut Sunday in Buffalo as the emergency third quarterback after Tyler Huntley also went down with a toe injury in the first half. Baltimore became the first team to have three quarterbacks throw a pass before halftime of a game since the 2017 Cowboys, per ESPN Research . That's before Jackson even entered the NFL. "That's a tough deal, and then the next guy [Huntley] as well [going down]," Head Coach Jesse Minter said. "I thought Joe came in – to his credit, not really getting a lot of reps in preparation – hung in there, did some good stuff." Amidst a blitz-happy Bills defense that stressed Baltimore's offensive line and with zero first-team reps in practice this week, Fagnano had tough sledding in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills. He was 10-of-21 for 91 passing yards, had one interception and lost one fumble. Even he dealt with a lower-body injury in the second half after an illegal hit. Now, with Jackson headed for surgery and injured reserve and Huntley's status unknown moving forward, Fagnano could make his first career start Thursday night against the first-place Jacksonville Jaguars at M&T Bank Stadium. "[I'll] control what I can control," Fagnano said. "If it is me and whoever's down or whatever it is, I'm just going to put my best foot forward and give the Ravens everything that I have. That's all I can do at the end of the day." Fagnano had a fantastic preseason in which he led all NFL quarterbacks with 509 passing yards in three games. He threw three touchdowns to one interception and posted a 100.4 passer rating. But playing a top team in a regular-season game when thrust into action is a tall task. Fagnano gave the Ravens' offense an immediate spark upon entering the game. He connected with rookie tight end Josh Cuevas for a 15-yard gain, then hit rookie wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane for a 13-yard pickup. The Ravens struggled to maintain momentum, however. Baltimore's offense mustered just 144 total yards and was 3-of-13 on third down. "It's tough to see Lamar go down like that," Fagnano said. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Custom image of Carnell Tate and Chase Brown. My Titans vs. Bengals prediction is the Over 46.5 after the Titans traded All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Bears on Thursday, leaving the Bengals 11.5-point favorites this afternoon. The Titans' defense was already last in DVOA at FTN before losing its anchor up front, while the Bengals are coming off a 35-13 win over the Ravens. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Paycor Stadium. Read the full analysis below, and find more winners in my NFL picks for Week 8. TOP PICK Titans vs Bengals prediction: Over 46.5 One of my first plays of Week 8 was taking the Over in this game. And with Jeffery Simmons swapping his trademark red sleeves for Chicago orange in a deal that has the Bears surging up the Super Bowl odds board , I like the Over even more, considering the Cincinnati Bengals will do the heavy lifting. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Ravens stop unit in the second half of last week's win. They finished with 7.0 yards per play and were a perfect 5 for 5 in the red zone, with Joe Burrow and his talented receiving corps finding their stride. The Titans' secondary allows the second-highest completion rate and has been burned by multiple big plays, bleeding the fourth-most passes of 20+ yards entering Week 8. While they haven't given up many passing touchdowns, they haven't faced many QBs on Burrow's level. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring, but don't discount the Titans. They're playing with pace and face a Bengals defense that still has work to do. Our Week 8 SGP roundup features a Titans vs. Bengals combo as well. Chase Brown finds the end zone to the cheers of fantasy owners everywhere. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins ' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Titans secondary giving up explosive plays. Chase Brown anytime touchdown Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards Titans vs Bengals touchdown scorer: Chase Brown If anyone was happy to see Simmons traded before Week 8, it was Bengals running back Brown. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Titans red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, the Titans had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. Due to that drought, we're getting a discount on his anytime touchdown market in Week 8, considering this prop was trading around 60% two games ago. Given the massive spread, the Bengals will be in a run-positive game script in the second half on Sunday, helping boost Brown's TD probabilities. His TD forecasts range between 60% and 78%, given he's a threat to run one in or catch a touchdown pass. For other options, browse our Week 8 anytime touchdown picks . Titans vs Bengals player prop: Tee Higgins 70+ receiving yards The Bengals have arguably the best one-two punch at receiver in the NFL, with Higgins serving as Robin to Ja'Marr Chase 's Batman. Just don't tell Higgins that. He looked more like Superman in Week 7, putting in a monster effort in the win over the rival Ravens. He caught six of seven balls his way for 148 yards and a touchdown. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. The Titans have also been burned by WR2s to start the season, ranking 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Higgins' Week 8 models are very bullish on his receiving yards, ranging from 65 to a high of 91. Most forecasts come in above 80 yards, and my projection sits just shy of 81 yards receiving. John Lanfranca Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:01 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) will host the Tennessee Titans (1-6) in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 13.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -950 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +640 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals pick: Bengals -13.5 (-110) My Bengals vs. Titans best bet is Cincinnati to cover the spread. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Titans vs Bengals NFL Odds Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +13.5 (-110), Titans -13.5 (-110) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-118o / 104u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +640, Bengals -950 Titans vs Bengals Preview for NFL Week 8 Tennessee Titans Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Cincinnati Bengals Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Picks, Betting Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. away.headline: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans
away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. home.headline: Bengals coach Zac Taylor updates the injury statuses of Cashius Howell, DJ Turner II and Cedric Johnson
home.blurb: But there is good injury news for the Bengals. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) and defensive end Cedric Johnson (ankle) are day-to-day, and Taylor said he expects Turner to travel to Spain with the team when they fly out on Tuesday. All three players were ruled out of the game vs. the Titans early in the fourth quarter with their respective injuries. But the fact that Turner in particular is a true day-to-day per Taylor is good news against a Falcons receiving corps led by Drake London, who is sixth in the NFL in receiving yards (624). CINCINNATI, Ohio — When the Bengals travel to Madrid to face the Falcons this coming Sunday, they will be without one of their young pass rushers. Zac Taylor confirmed to reporters that rookie defensive end Cashius Howell had wrist surgery on Sunday night, hours after the Bengals’ 43-36 overtime win against the Titans . He didn’t confirm that Howell will go on injured reserve but that he is “probably trending in that direction.” Howell’s injury means more opportunities for his fellow former Texas A&M defensive end Shemar Stewart, who played against the Titans after being a healthy scratch a week prior against the Ravens. “Shemar has just been doing everything he can to control his spot, and we trust him to go in there to make some plays for us,” Taylor said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. away.headline: Ravens linked with Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett after benching, Lamar Jackson injury
away.blurb: Shortly after it was learned on Sunday that Baltimore Ravens starting quarterback Lamar Jackson could miss the rest of this season after he suffered an injury to the thumb on his throwing hand during the club's 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills that left him needing surgery, a report linked the Ravens with current Chicago Bears backup Tyson Bagent . However, that same story noted that "it won’t be cheap" for the desperate Ravens to acquire Bagent ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline. According to Ravens and league reporter Jason La Canfora of Sports Illustrated and other outlets, the Arizona Cardinals may have a cheaper option for Baltimore. Ravens are reportedly "interested" in Jacoby Brissett after Lamar Jackson injury Specifically, La Canfora spoke with an unnamed "high-ranking official from another NFL club" who suggested that the Ravens could call the Cardinals about journeyman quarterback Jacoby Brissett . "That's the other name I heard they are interested in, besides the back-up in Chicago," the official said about the Ravens and Brissett. Ravens backup signal-caller Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in Baltimore's loss to Buffalo on Sunday, and La Canfora mentioned that Huntley "likely" won't be good to go for when the 4-4 Ravens host the 5-2 Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday evening. Additionally, La Canfora shared that Baltimore emergency option Joe Fagnano needed treatment for his ankle/foot throughout the second half of Sunday's loss. On paper, Brissett would be an upgrade over a healthy Fagnano. Why Cardinals may be willing to now dump Jacoby Brissett As for Brissett, he was benched in favor of backup Gardner Minshew II during Arizona's matchup at the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and Minshew helped the Cardinals earn a 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys. While Arizona improved to 3-5, La Canfora mentioned that "execs around the NFL expect the Cardinals, in a rebuild, to move veterans before the trade deadline." It's assumed that first-year Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur will eventually want to get a look at rookie quarterback Carson Beck before Week 18 arrives. Presumably, the Cardinals could trade Brissett to the Ravens and start Minshew until Arizona's Week 14 bye. The Cardinals could then use that break to get Beck ready to start unless Minshew keeps Arizona in the playoff hunt through the middle of December. Want more articles like this? All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players. The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams. Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field. Lions 23, Vikings 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions. The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week. Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league. I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . picks.headline: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8
picks.blurb: Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Bold predictions for the Vikings against the Lions in Week 8 Cole Smith, Vikings Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 4:25 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (6-0) own the longest active winning streak in the NFL. Dating back to November 30, 2025, they have won 11 games in a row, leaning on an exceptional defense and offense that emphasizes ball control. On Sunday, they head to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions (4-2), who have won two straight and are looking to stay within striking distance of the NFC North lead. The Lions' strengths are the opposite of the Vikings', ranking 2nd in scoring offense and yards per game through seven games, while no one is allowing more yards than Detroit. Minnesota's last four wins have come against teams with a combined record of 7-20. The Lions are the first opponent in a tough four-game stretch where the Vikings will play the Bills , Packers, and 49ers. Skeptics are waiting for Minnesota to come crashing back to Earth, and Sunday could be the first evidence of a regression if the Vikings' offense can't score some points. Here are three bold predictions for the Vikings' matchup against the Lions. Kyler Murray will throw for over 300 yards One way you know you're making a bold prediction is if you can visualize people closing out of your article after reading. Minnesota's offense ranks 29th in passing yards. While Kyler Murray has avoided turnovers (two interceptions on 125 attempts), he hasn't consistently attacked defenses downfield. Kevin O'Connell said after last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts that the Vikings' offense is " not far off " from finding its footing. Four runs on the opening drive led to a turnover on downs, and a 3rd-and-5 on Minnesota's second drive ended in an incompletion when RG Will Fries pushed into Murray, who was ready to fire to a wide-open Justin Jefferson. Although the Vikings' defense has been elite since their 11-game winning streak began, O'Connell knows the offense will need to score to keep up with their next four opponents. Expect Murray to be less gunshy on Sunday, but here's hoping that doesn't result in recklessness. Murray goes for over 300, providing optimism moving forward that this passing attack can return to its pre-2025 self. The Vikings will intercept Jared Goff Like Murray, Lions QB Jared Goff has avoided turnovers this year. He has not thrown an interception through six games. However, Goff has still managed to complete 67.3% of his passes for 1,788 yards and 14 touchdowns for an offense that is tied for 4th-best in EPA/play. I'm not sure Minnesota can completely shut down this year's Goff, but they'll pressure him and force him into some bad plays. When the two teams last played, the Vikings forced Goff to turn the ball over five times (two interceptions, three fumbles). It may be difficult to replicate that production, but look for Brian Flores to flummox Goff into at least an extra possession. The Vikings will stop a fourth-down conversion Minnesota was somewhat susceptible to critical conversion attempts last week against Indianapolis. They allowed the Colts to convert 8-of-15 third-down attempts and their lone fourth-down attempt. Detroit converted 5-of-10 third-down attempts against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 but went 0-for-2 on fourth-down, including a controversial 4th-and-1 attempt from their own 24-yard line. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that fear of stopping the Packers' offense and gaining another possession played into last week's decision. away.headline: Kyler Murray Injured, Latest Updates on Vikings QB's Hamstring, Status vs. Bills in NFL Week 9
away.blurb: He was unable to return to the game and finished his first game as a Viking with just 18 passing yards, nine rushing yards and an interception. The Minnesota Vikings got some bad news about their starting quarterback on Monday. Coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters Kyler Murray came away from the 19-15 defeat to the Detroit Lions with a hamstring issue. The full extent of his injury isn't yet known. Murray's tenure with the Vikings got off to a rough start in Week 1, as he was forced to exit against the Green Bay Packers in Minnesota's third offensive drive. He attempted to slide while scrambling and took a hard hit from Javon Bullard. Luckily for the Vikings, veteran quarterback Carson Wentz came in and threw for 133 yards and three touchdowns, helping Minnesota come back from a 12-point deficit to win 37-22 and start the season on the right note. Murray is coming off an injury-filled 2025 campaign that saw him play just five games for the Arizona Cardinals as he finished the season with 962 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions. He signed with the Vikings in March and later won the starting quarterback job, hoping to get a fresh start. Unfortunately for him, his season started with an injury, and his performance since returning has been inconsistent. If Murray has to miss time, Wentz will presumably elevate into the starting role for Week 9 matchup with the Buffalo Bills.
