away.headline: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
away.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return) Skip to main content SI.COM Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions. Vikings who could return in Week 8 Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time. The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week. Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year. With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota. Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup. Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly. If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field. Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run . Now the Jets host another franchise on a losing streak, the Las Vegas Raiders , who are on a four-game skid following a 3-0 start. They didn't take advantage versus the Dolphins, and I don't think they do so in this spot either. The Raiders offense with Cousins still under center and led by the trio of Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty and Tre Tucker is too much to handle for this underwhelming Jets' defense to overcome. Gang Green drops to 2-6 on the season, with questions about head coach Aaron Glenn's future only growing as the losses continue to mount. Jets' takeaways in deflating loss: What we learned in Jets' 28-25 upset loss at home to winless Dolphins Mike Dougherty The pick: Jets 27, Raiders 24 Here's why: Geno Smith will be motivated to make something positive happen. After last week's failures, the rest of the locker room has to feel additional urgency to quiet the noise. More importantly, the Raiders have struggled to run the ball and struggled to stop the run. The pick: Raiders 30, Jets 17 Here's why: There's nowhere to go but up for Gang Green but it might take some time to see that movement. The pick: Raiders 23, Jets 20 Here's why: The Jets weren't able to take care of business against the winless Dolphins team last week, so it's difficult to pick them this week, even against a team that's struggling as well. The pick: Raiders 27, Jets 17 Here's why: Aaron Glenn's weekly game management blunders seemed to finally take a toll on the entire team in the Jets' brutal effort against the Dolphins. With the Jets operating with a coaching disadvantage, it's hard to be confident in them in any game moving forward. The pick: Jets 20, Raiders 17 Here's why: It's hard to explain, it just feels like this is the type of game the Jets unexplainably win and becomes a terrible loss for the Raiders. picks.headline: Raiders vs Jets game picks: Who the staff has winning Week 8 matchup
picks.blurb: Raiders vs Jets game picks: Who the staff has winning Week 8 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Raiders vs Jets game picks: Who the staff has winning Week 8 matchup Levi Damien, Marvin Uzor, Lance Fernandez and LaMarr Fields, Raiders Wire Fri, October 30, 2026 at 2:30 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week the Raiders head to the Meadowlands in New Jersey to face the New York Jets. Neither team is looking too hot at the moment. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak and the Jets just lost to the previously winless Dolphins . To get a feel for how this one could play out, we get the takes from the Raiders Wire staff. Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. However, playing against a defense that has surrendered the fourth-most points per game and playing at home should give New York's offense a boost. That and the Jets' solid pass defense should keep the Raiders' losing streak going. Marvin Uzor -- Raiders 24, Jets 20 The Jets have been the NFL's slowest-starting offense since last season, so this is the week the Raiders finally don't have to dig out of an early hole. Put Kirk Cousins against a defense with one interception in 24 games, and I think the losing streak ends at four. Lamarr Fields -- Raiders 24. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. Levi Damien -- Raiders 20, Jets 19 Nothing about this Raiders team right now inspires confidence in me. And it isn't because they've lost four straight. It's the manner in which they lost them. Either just getting flat out streamrolled or giving up a ton of points and then trying to make a comeback when it's too late. The offensive line is starting to look like who we thought they were and the defense simply doesn't look smart. And playing on the east coast? Ugh. That being said, I have less confidence in Geno Smith. Perhaps that comes from the experience with him in Las Vegas last season, who knows. But I think the Jets record reflects that he's not the answer, with their only wins coming over a hapless Titans team and a low-scoring affair against the Browns. And they're coming off handing the Dolphins their first win of the season. The same Dolphins team the Raiders put a hurting on in the opener. I see a close one here. picks.headline: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8
picks.blurb: Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Jets vs. Raiders: 5 bold predictions for Week 8 Geoffrey A Knox, Jets Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 12:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets are running out of opportunities to turn their season around, and Sunday's matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders presents a chance to stop the bleeding. At 2-5, Aaron Glenn's team has lost two straight games, including a frustrating divisional defeat against the previously winless Miami Dolphins . Another setback would make an already disappointing season considerably more difficult to salvage. Fortunately for New York, the Raiders aren't exactly arriving in peak condition. Las Vegas has dropped four consecutive games after opening the season 3-0, and its recent offensive struggles have created some questions of its own. Neither team can afford another afternoon of wasted opportunities, making this an interesting matchup between two teams looking to rediscover their footing. There are reasons to believe the Jets can finally put together a complete performance at MetLife Stadium. Here are five bold predictions for Week 8. Geno Smith and Garrett Wilson connect for 100-plus receiving yards and a touchdown Garrett Wilson, Jets fans, and plenty of people covering the team will be happy campers after this one. Wilson has too often been an afterthought in an offense that needs its best playmakers involved, and Sunday presents an opportunity to change that narrative. Smith and Wilson connect for more than 100 receiving yards, with the star wideout finding the end zone. After all the discussion about getting Wilson more opportunities, the Jets finally make that connection a central part of their offensive production. Ashton Jeanty finishes with fewer than 65 rushing yards Ashton Jeanty ran for 102 yards in the Raiders ' season opener, but he hasn't come close to that production since. He hasn't exceeded 58 rushing yards in any subsequent game, and his highest rushing total over Las Vegas' last three outings was just 27 yards. Now he faces a Jets defense that he decided to publicly criticize before the game. Jeanty questioned whether some New York defenders actually want to tackle, so the motivation factor shouldn't be difficult to find. The Jets respond by limiting him to 65 yards or fewer, making the Raiders running back work for everything he gets. The Jets intercept Kirk Cousins Cousins threw three interceptions combined during the first two weeks of the season before posting a clean outing in Week 3. Since then, he's developed an alternating pattern of games with an interception and games without one. He avoided a turnover against Kansas City in Week 7, which puts him in line for another costly mistake. The Jets' defense has playmakers capable of taking advantage when opposing quarterbacks become careless. Cousins has already demonstrated that he can put the football in harm's way, and New York breaks up his turnover-free streak by coming away with an interception. New York rushes for 150 yards and a touchdown The Jets enter Week 8 averaging 96.4 rushing yards per game, while Las Vegas has surrendered 143.6 yards per contest. That is a substantial difference in production, and New York has an opportunity to take advantage of a defense that has struggled to contain opposing ground attacks. The prediction calls for 150 rushing yards and at least one touchdown. Establishing the run would also help take pressure off Smith, give the offense some balance and make the Raiders defend the entire field rather than simply anticipating another passing attempt. The Jets win a back-and-forth affair New York has scored at least 23 points in three games this season. In its other four outings, the offense has failed to reach 19 points, making consistency a significant concern heading into Sunday. The Raiders need this victory just as badly, having lost four straight, so neither team should lack motivation. This one turns into a back-and-forth affair, with both offenses finding enough production to keep the outcome in doubt late. Ultimately, the Jets make a few more plays when it matters and escape with a much-needed victory. Prediction: Jets 27, Raiders 24. away.blurb: The second injury report is out for the Raiders and Jets for their Week 8 matchup. On it the Raiders had a couple upgrades, while all the players the Jets were missing to injury are still missing. Including sacks leader David Bailey. For the Raiders, the only player missing was reserve DE Patrick Johnson (stinger). Still limited was DT Foley Fatukasi (shoulder), OT DJ Glaze (ankle) and TE Ian Thomas (shoulder). The big name is obviously Bailey who is the team's top pass rusher with 5.5 sacks on the season. He was the team's pick at number two overall out of Texas Tech. So, if he can't go, that's a pretty big deal. #Raiders #Jets Thursday injury report They saw upgrades to full participation from TE Brock Bowers (knee) and LB Quay Walker (chest). There were four players missing on Wednesday for the Jets, and all four were still missing. Those players were EDGE David Bailey (groin), EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), OL Max Mitchell (concussion), and DL T'Vondre Sweat (knee). away.headline: Raiders Open Jets Week With Great Injury Report News
away.blurb: Las Vegas appears to be getting healthier after several players participated in Wednesday's practice on a limited basis. That included Brock Bowers, Folorunso Fatukasi, DJ Glaze, Kwity Paye, Ian Thomas, and Quay Walker. Patrick Johnson did not participate in Wednesday's practice. Thursday's injury report featured many of the same names, with improved statuses. Bowers, Paye, and Walker fully participated in Thursday's practice. Patrick Johnson did not practice again on Thursday. Fatukasi, Glaze, and Thomas again practiced on a limited basis on Thursday. “I would start with the energy he brings to our team, his love of the game, his work habits. He just has a whole other aura about him when he’s on the field, and his teammates feel it. Coaches feel it. He’s a really solid run blocker; he’s got strong hands. Really happy to have him back out there,” Kubiak said earlier this week. Raiders Open Jets Week With Great Injury Report News Skip to main content SI.COM The Las Vegas Raiders have lost four straight and are looking for any bit of momentum they can find heading into Week 8. Their matchup against the New York Jets is enough reason to be cautiously optimistic about their chances, but several other factors raise concerns. Along with playing much earlier than they are used to, the Raiders face multiple foundational issues heading into Sunday. They are not in a position to think Sunday against the Jets will be a cakewalk, regardless of the Jets' record. Geno Smith would love to add to Las Vegas' woes. Tight end Carter Runyon was listed on Las Vegas' Wednesday injury report with a foot injury as he returned to practice from Injured Reserve. He fully participated in Wednesday's and Thursday's practices. Injuries or not, the Raiders have plenty of issues they need to clean up on offense and defense. Klint Kubiak said the coaches have held the players accountable, and the players have done a solid job of holding each other accountable. The Raiders need more than just accountability, though. “That’s the NFL. Every week you have to respond, and you’ve got to do it 17 weeks in a row. You can’t sit in those chairs in those team meeting rooms if you’re not an accountable human. If you’re just a talented guy who doesn’t have accountability, you don’t last very long. Those are the guys we’re looking for as we build our program,” Kubiak said earlier this week. It will be up to Kubiak and his coaching staff to press the right buttons this week to shake things up. Las Vegas has not had the answers in any of the past four weeks. With their roster getting healthier heading into Week 8, the Raiders must take care of business against the Jets. The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Oct 11, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) carries the ball in the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. picks.headline: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns
picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joey Bray Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between the teams on Thursday Night Football. However, the Steelers have rattled off three straight wins since then. The winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the second half of the regular season. With both teams coming off wins and identical records, FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Pittsburgh Steelers the slight edge as a 3.5-point favorite over Cleveland. This is as close to a "must-win" game in the middle of the season for the Steelers as we will ever see. With all of that being said, here are some predictions based around my favorite prop bets of the weekend. Germie Bernard over 43.5 receiving yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Wide receiver Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates the first down in the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images This number is ridiculously low because the rookie receiver will be one of, if not the most targeted pass catchers on the entire team on Sunday. Last time these two teams met, Bernard got barely any playing time, but that gives him the chance to take advantage of a group that hasn't seen what he can do yet. In their first matchup, Pittsburgh had two receivers go over this total. I'm not letting last game scare me, as the Steelers controlled the clock running the football, leading to limited opportunities for any receiver. It would be a shock to see no receiver have more than three catches for the second week in a row. Bernard is a volume receiver that the Steelers will need to rely on to get open and break some tackles against their tough man defense. Rico Dowdle gets over 70 scrimmage yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Ifeatu Melifonwu #5 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles Rico Dowdle #13 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ever since running back Rico Dowdle has returned to the lineup from his toe injury, he has looked significantly more efficient with the ball in his hands. Sure, the improved offensive line helps, but Dowdle is going to continue to earn more runs in the offense with his numbers improving. Last week, the veteran back averaged a season-high 4.6 yards per carry. Dowdle also hauled in six passes, good for the most on the team, for 45 yards. It was a more even share of the opportunities for the Steelers running backs, as Dowdle had 16 touches compared to Jaylen Warren's 21. Dowdle is the change of pace back in the Steelers offense, but is one that they will continue to use quite a bit as he gets healthier. Warren's breakout doesn't mean that Dowdle won't be involved in the offense. In fact, I think what we saw against New Orleans is what we can expect from Dowdle for the rest of the season. With the browns struggles to defend the run, both backs could be in for a big day on Sunday. Darnell Washington continues dominance with a touchdown TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Darnell Washington #80 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a pass from Aaron Rodgers #8 during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers' six-foot-seven tight end has already set career highs in total touchdowns this season. His increased usage in the red zone is something Steelers fans have been begging to see for years now. Last week, Washington dunked on Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry as he snatched the ball out of the air from four yards out for the Steelers' only touchdown in Paris. The tight end has caught a touchdown pass in two consecutive games, and I have a hard time seeing that trend stopping against Cleveland given his continued usage in the red zone. Washington also scored against the Browns in their first matchup a month ago. It almost makes too much sense to see Washington in the end zone again on Sunday. What are your predictions for Steelers vs. Browns in their Week 8 matchup? Let us know what you think in the comments . picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game Curt Popejoy, Steelers Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns square off, both teams at 5-2 and tied on top in the AFC North. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North. Final score prediction: Steelers 35, Browns 24 This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game

picks.headline: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Steelers vs. Browns: Week 8 game picks (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jarrett Bailey Sat, October 31, 2026 at 3:19 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads First place in the AFC North is up for grabs as the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Cleveland Browns. Both teams enter the day at 5-2, with Cleveland holding a 1-0 head-to-head advantage over Pittsburgh. Will they beat the Steelers on the road in a regular season game for the first time since 2003? Our staff weighs in. Mike Nicastro : The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns twice in a season in almost three decades, but this year presents a unique challenge. Teams traveling internationally over the last two seasons are just 1-7 when returning to face a team that did not travel overseas the prior week. That one win was the Broncos last season, when they scored 33 4th quarter points against the Giants to win by 1 point. Fatigue will play a factor, but having home field will help significantly. This is still a Browns team that lost to the Jets on the road, and just went to the wire with the Titans. Won't be surprised if its ugly, but Pittsburgh rides the run game again into their bye. Steelers 20 Browns 17. Jason Aponte: This will be a dogfight between the division rivals. The Steelers have shown improvement offensively lately and will need to beat Cleveland's plan of man coverage. Rodgers and the offense does enough and the defense holds up to give Pittsburgh the division lead. Steelers 21, Browns 17. Ryan Parish : The Steelers were the better team in 3 out of 4 quarters the last time these teams met a few weeks ago. Both teams have found a groove since, and they enter the contest at 5-2. Winner leaves the game atop the AFC North. I've had a running bit in these predictions that will not change until it stops working. Browns 24-Steelers 23. Austin Bechtold: The Steelers haven't lost to the Browns at home in the regular season since I was two. I can't fathom it happening with how the Steelers defense is playing right now. I've been wrong about Patrick Graham and doubted his scheme to a degree early in the season, but if he calls a great gameplan Sunday I'm sold. Aaron Rodgers is playing his best football since 2021. The Browns aren't the old Browns and I think are better than people are giving credit for. The Steelers do what it takes, and will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North on Sunday. Steelers 24-18. Ryland Bickley : This is a series that has been defined by home teams winning as of late, and with the Steelers on a hot streak and playing in Acrisure this Sunday, I don't expect that to change. Cleveland's man coverage scheme should once again prove a challenge for the Pittsburgh offense, but the Steelers defense has taken some strides since the last matchup. Steelers 27, Browns 20 . Joey Bray : When these teams take the field on Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers will be exactly one month removed from suffering another loss to the Browns in Cleveland on Thursday Night Football. Since that game, the Steelers have won three straight. I can't say for certain how much the team has grown since then, as they still have concerns in the secondary on defense and struggles in the red zone as an offense. Unlike last time where the browns jumped out to a big lead early, I think this game will be a close one throughout. The Browns are a much better football team that anyone anticipated entering the season. Todd Monken deserves a ton of credit for the way he has continued to put Deshaun Watson and the offense in positions to win. However, all five of their wins have come on game winning drives, a trend that is unlikely to continue. I'll take Pittsburgh to get their revenge on Cleveland and go into the bye week with sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Steelers 21, Browns 20 . Jarrett Bailey: I said ahead of the Saints game that I don't know if the Steelers are a team I'd bank on winning four games in a row, yet here we are after a three-game win streak. The whole "Cleveland hasn't won in Pittsburgh since 2003" doesn't necessarily mean much to me in terms of results. Although it does seem to matter when these two teams play in Cleveland that the Steelers turn into the worst versions of themselves. I do think the Steelers win, but I'm not going to take this Browns team lightly. Steelers 20, Browns 16. Let us know what you think in the comments . One possibility is the return of Pittman Jr. following the week off. Speaking to the media the day after the team's Week 8 victory, the veteran receiver shared an encouraging update and some more information on his current injury. He wasn't able to say for sure, but he shared that he would love to return following the bye week. "It would be great to be back after the bye week, which is what I would like," he told reporters. "But I can't go out there if I'm not effective. So, only time will tell." "Trying to get back out there as fast as possibl and prove to this team that I came to better it and not just sit on the sidelines." picks.headline: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions
picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. Atlanta cannot afford to get away from what worked against San Francisco. Establishing the run will help take pressure off Penix while creating opportunities for the offense to control the game. Defensively, the Falcons need to make enough key stops and force the Buccaneers into difficult situations. Tampa Bay is capable of making plays offensively, but Atlanta has shown improvements on that side of the ball. Coming off last week’s momentum-building victory over the 49ers, I like the Falcons to carry that confidence into Tampa. It won’t be easy, but Atlanta does enough on both sides of the ball to earn a hard-fought divisional victory, take over first place in the NFC South, and leave Tampa Bay with a win. Prediction: Falcons 24, Buccaneers 17 Garrett Chapman (3-4) The Falcons are fresh off their biggest win of the season, but they have to take the show on the road on Sunday. They've had a lot of success in Tampa over the last few years, and this team will enter with a lot of confidence with how Michael Penix has been playing. This will be a tight game that I expect will come down to the final drive. The Buccaneer defense is solid, and it will be a difficult test on the road for an offense that hasn't shown it can consistently be a steady unit. Atlanta has a chance to take over the top spot in the NFC South on Sunday, but it won't happen just yet. picks.blurb: Our Buccaneers vs. Falcons Score Predictions Are In Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have a must-win game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. A win puts them within striking distance of the Carolina Panthers for the division lead, while a loss would put them even further behind this season. It should be a close one against a better Falcons team, and our panel of writers reflect that. Here are our picks for Tampa Bay's big matchup against Atlanta: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Falcons 24, Bucs 23 Despite the Bucs' dismantling of the Panthers last week, I still find it difficult to have much confidence in them heading into the matchup against the rising Atlanta Falcons. The offense can only lean on the run game for so long, so they must figure out how to attack defenses through the air. The defense and special teams have been great as of late and will need to show up in a big way again. While I do think the Bucs have a better shot at beating the Falcons now than I did a couple of weeks ago, I think the Falcons' defense will find a way to slow down the run game and force the Bucs to throw the ball. That hasn’t been great for them this year, and ultimately will be the downfall of them this week. Overall Record: 4-3 James Hill, Writer: Falcons 21, Bucs 17 Despite having a fantastic game last week, I think the Buccaneers will come back down to earth in this matchup. I don’t believe Baker Mayfield is fully healthy yet, and they drop this one because of it. Overall Record: 3-4 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Bucs 24, Falcons 21 The Buccaneers and Falcons are a fun matchup. Todd Bowles' defense has really turned it up in recent weeks, while the Falcons have several dangerous weapons on offense. Assuming Mayfield’s thumb feels quite a bit better than it did a week ago, I think the Bucs’ offense can do just enough to squeeze out a victory while extending the Bucs’ record to 2-0 in the division and narrowing the gap between them and the NFC South-leading Panthers. Logan Robinson, Founder: Bucs 28, Falcons 23 I think the Bucs do end up winning this game, and it has to do with Todd Bowles’ rush defense, which has been excellent this year. Adding that with strong secondary play and getting Antoine Winfield Jr. back to help defend Atlanta’s passing attack, it looks nice. It’s going to be a close one, but I like Tampa Bay and a bold prediction of Cade Otton having a good showing. River Wells, Editor: Falcons 24, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay didn't have to pass much against the Carolina Panthers to beat them. Atlanta has a strong rushing defense, so they won't let the Bucs beat them that way — Tampa Bay will have to go through the air. I'm still not confident that Zac Robinson's offense can do that against this Falcons team. Baker Mayfeld is still recovering from injury and BIjan Robinson can change games on his own — Bucs drop this one in Raymond James. Consensus: Falcons 3, Bucs 2 This is among the closest prediction slates we've had all year. Some of us believe the Bucs will keep the momentum going, while other writers think Tampa Bay will falter as it has multiple times this year. The Bucs play the Falcons at 1 p.m. in Tampa Bay on Nov. 1. I trust this Tampa Bay defense, which ranks in the top five in DVOA against both the pass and the run. The Buccaneers are second in EPA per dropback and fifth in Rush EPA. However, the winner of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' Week 8 battle with the Atlanta Falcons will likely determine who is the favorite to win the division. At 2-5, the Bucs have been left for dead more than once this season. However, their 43-13 annihilation of the first-place Carolina Panthers has them right back in the thick of the division race. Now only one game out of first place, Tampa's season has officially risen from the dead. If the Bucs can beat the 3-4 Falcons on Sunday, they will be only half a game behind the Panthers, who fell to 3-4 with their loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday. However, securing a victory over Atlanta will be no easy task. The Falcons are marching into Raymond James Stadium on a high note after their 29-20 win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers last week. This crucial NFC South showdown will have a big say in who takes the division crown this season and features two teams that have walked similar paths through the season's first seven weeks. The Bucs and Falcons both had high expectations coming into the season. Both teams have talented rosters and were hoping to break free of their recent curse of mediocrity. Like the Bucs, the Falcons fell flat coming out of the gate. After two straight losses to start the season, including an embarrassing 34-3 home defeat to the Panthers in Week 2, Atlanta looked like the league's worst team. However, those losses came with starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and backup Tua Tagovailoa both injured. The Falcons were forced to start third-string Cooper Rush in the first two games before he was benched for Jack Strand. Penix returned in Week 3 and led Atlanta to a dominant 35-14 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, followed by a 45-24 thrashing of the New Orleans Saints on the road in Week 4. In those victories, plus last week's triumph over the 49ers, the Falcons have looked like a legitimate playoff team. The Bucs have also looked like a bottom-feeder for much of the season. However, in their demolition of the Panthers and a Week 5 road upset over the Dallas Cowboys , the Bucs have also looked like a playoff team. Both teams have taken turns as Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde this season. Which version of each team will we see on Sunday? In my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory , I highlighted the need for Tampa's defense to contain superstar Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson and to find a way to stop tight end Kyle Pitts, who has been a Buc-killer his entire career. If the Bucs can do both, they have a great chance to earn their third victory of the season. If not, it could be a long afternoon for the home team. The Bucs must also give their own star RB, Bucky Irving, a healthy workload to control the clock and keep the potent Atlanta offense on the sidelines. If Irving gets 20+ touches and Baker Mayfield takes care of the ball in his second game back from a three-game absence with a broken thumb, the offense should have success. I believe the Bucs' defense, which has been strong all year, will slow the Falcons offense just enough for Tampa to get its second straight victory. I think a late Penix interception will seal the game for the Bucs. Prediction: Bucs 30, Falcons 24

away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. away.headline: Falcons-Bucs Inactives | Antoine Winfield Jr. Makes His Return
away.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has missed three games thanks to a rib injury suffered against Green Bay in Week Four, but he is cleared to play on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons and expected to start. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, however, was ruled out on Friday and will be sidelined for the second game in a row by a foot injury. He had previously been listed with a concussion as well but was able to clear the league's concussion protocol late in the week. Tackle Luke Goedeke will also return to action after missing one game with a calf injury. Goedeke did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned during Friday's session in a limited capacity. The Buccaneers and Falcons submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Eight meeting at Raymond James Stadium. The Buccaneers did not make any practice squad elevations this week and thus have 53 available players on Sunday, meaning they had to name five inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Falcons elevated linebacker Brian Asamoah and running back Khalil Herbert from their practice squad and therefore had to name seven players inactive for the game. Atlanta's offense will be without it's complementary backfield weapon for Bijan Robinson, as Brian Robinson is out due toa hamstring injury. Starting linebacker Divine Deablo will also miss the game due to a forearm injury, though fellow starter Kendal Daniels was cleared after missing some practice time due to an Achilles tendon ailment. Cornerback Billy Bowman will join Deablo on the sideline thanks to a hamstring strain, but cornerback Avieon Terrell, who was considered questionable for the game due to illness is good to go. home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Thursday injury report for Week 8
home.blurb: There was some encouraging news for Tampa Bay, as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (illness) and linebacker Josiah Trotter (illness) were both upgraded to full participation after being limited and sidelined, respectively, during Wednesday's practice. Running back Kenny Gainwell (hip) also showed improvement, returning to practice in a limited capacity after sitting out Wednesday. However, offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) remained sidelined for a second consecutive day, leaving his availability for Sunday's game uncertain. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was limited for the second straight practice as he continues working through his injuries. Wide receivers Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving did not practice due to scheduled rest, while defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson was limited for the same reason. Meanwhile, Atlanta saw several players return to practice Thursday. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) were both upgraded to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith also returned in a limited capacity after receiving a rest day Wednesday. Running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) remained the Falcons' lone non-participant Thursday due to injury. Atlanta continued to have several players limited, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, providing a clearer picture of which players could be unavailable for Sunday's matchup. home.headline: Atlanta Falcons @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Who's On The Injury Report?
home.blurb: Backup running back Brian Robinson Jr. had already missed Week Seven against the San Francisco 49ers with a hamstring injury. That injury lingers, and he is out this week. Khalil Herbert will continue to back up starting running back Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was downgraded to out with a hamstring injury. With veteran safety Jessie Bates III , veteran defensive back Sydney Brown, and young safety Xavier Watts making the middle of the field a tough place to play for opposing offenses, Bowman Jr. has enough reinforcements to heal. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out again with a foot injury. Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been a one-two punch for Tampa this year, with almost identical stats. The main difference is that Egbuka has the touchdowns, with two this season. We will see how much that affects Tampa's offense on Sunday. Backup running back Kenny Gainwell and offensive tackle Luke Goedeke are both questionable and could also miss Sunday's game, hindering the offense. Egbuka (foot) did not participate in Friday's practice after being limited Wednesday and Thursday. The rookie receiver has cleared concussion protocol, but his lingering foot injury will keep him sidelined for a second consecutive game. Offensive tackle Luke Goedeke (calf) returned to practice on a limited basis Friday after missing the previous two sessions. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, along with running back Kenny Gainwell (hip), who was a full participant after steadily improving throughout the week. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby and linebacker Josiah Trotter, who were both dealing with illnesses earlier in the week, also practiced fully Friday and are expected to be available. Meanwhile, Atlanta will be without running back Brian Robinson, who was ruled out with a hamstring injury after missing all three practices this week. Charlie Disturco Sun, November 1, 2026 at 5:26 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts (2-5) and Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) will meet in Week 8 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Florida. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Jaguars are 10.5-point favorites over the Colts on the spread, with the total set at over/under 46.5 points. Jacksonville is a -520 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Indianapolis is a +400 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Colts vs Jaguars prediction and player prop pick for today's game. Colts vs Jaguars pick: Bhayshul Tuten Over 64.5 Rushing Yards (-111) My Jaguars vs. Colts best bet is Bhayshul Tuten to record over 64.5 rushing yards. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Colts vs Jaguars NFL Odds Colts vs Jaguars Spread : Colts +10.5 (-122), Jaguars -10.5 (+100) Colts vs Jaguars Total : over/under 45.5 (-106o / -114u) Colts vs Jaguars Moneyline : Colts +400, Jaguars -520 Colts vs Jaguars Preview for NFL Week 8 Indianapolis Colts Preview: Everything for Sale The fire sale is officially on in Indianapolis. Following a third consecutive loss, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson ( Seahawks ) and DeForest Buckner ( 49ers ). Josh Downs has also requested a trade, while all eyes have shifted toward the team's prized possession: superstar running back Jonathan Taylor . For now, there are no expected changes at quarterback. Colts head coach Shane Steichen doubled down on Daniel Jones , who threw for just 108 yards last week. The veteran quarterback has struggled mightily this season, throwing more interceptions (7) than touchdowns (4) while posting a career-low completion rate of 59.6%. There is some positive news for Indianapolis, however. Tyler Warren is expected to return to the starting lineup after missing two games with a groin injury. The same goes for Sauce Gardner , while Downs will also suit up despite his trade request. Warren's presence is a must for a Colts receiving room that includes 34-year-old Keenan Allen and journeyman Laquon Treadwell . The question remains: Can the Colts weather the storm and put up a fight against their division rival? The biggest question is how the offensive line will hold up against a formidable Jaguars defense. Indianapolis ranks around league average in rushing yards per game, but those numbers came with Nelson anchoring the offensive line. Taylor is already averaging a career-low 4.2 yards per carry, and losing another key piece up front certainly won't help. The Colts defense has its own issues, ranking in the bottom 10 in points allowed per game and 11th in rushing yards allowed (124.4). Rush defense is definitely Indy's Achilles' heel on the defensive end, ranking 29th in rushing EPA allowed. The pass defense, however, has been surprisingly solid. Indianapolis hasn't allowed a wide receiver room to reach 100 receiving yards since Week 4, while opposing receivers are averaging just 10 receptions per game. Jacksonville Jaguars Preview: Bhayshul Tuten Due for Breakout Game It was a much-needed bye week for the Jaguars, who are coming off two London games filled with late-game theatrics. Jacksonville's defense has been its strong suit this season. Outside of the Texans (34 points), no team has scored more than 17 against this talented unit. The Jaguars rank No. 1 in rushing yards allowed per game (72.2) but have struggled mightily against the pass, ranking 30th while surrendering 274 yards per game. Ultimately, Jacksonville's success will hinge on Trevor Lawrence and the offense finding another gear. The Jaguars are around league average in total offensive production and have maintained a near 50-50 split between the passing and running games. I'd be surprised if Jacksonville's ground game doesn't start to take off soon as Bhayshul Tuten is on the verge of a breakout. The explosive running back possesses elite speed and has already shown the ability to rip off chunk plays. Unfortunately, several of those big gains have been wiped away by holding penalties. Still, Tuten has rushed for at least 65 yards in five of his six games this season. I've been waiting for this offense to take the next step, and there are plenty of weapons to make it happen. Outside of Tuten, Jacksonville has a talented receiving corps led by Parker Washington . We also saw Travis Hunter become more involved offensively before the bye, recording four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. That increased usage is a trend I expect to continue in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr. has also been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the upcoming deadline. He was benched for the second half against Houston and hasn't recorded a catch in either of Jacksonville's last two games, making his involvement worth watching. One situation worth monitoring is Jakobi Meyers , who enters Sunday questionable after missing Friday's practice with hamstring and ankle injuries. Thomas would likely be relied on to step up in his absence. Another development I've highlighted previously is Jacksonville's increased use of two-tight-end sets. Brenton Strange has been nothing short of excellent, but the emergence of Nate Boerkircher could be just as important moving forward. The second-round pick played a career-high 55% of the snaps before the bye, and I expect his workload to consistently settle in the 50–60% range. Colts vs Jaguars Picks, Betting Analysis I hinted at it earlier, but I expect the Jaguars' ground game to take off. To me, it's a matter of when, not if. Tuten is PFF's No. 1-ranked running back and ranks among the league's best in yards after contact per carry. He draws a Colts run defense that has struggled all season and will be without one of its most important defensive players in Buckner. With Jacksonville entering this matchup as a double-digit favorite, I expect the Jaguars to control possession and lean heavily on the ground game. That should mean a healthy workload for Tuten. Coming off a bye, Tuten should be fresh and ready to take advantage of a spiraling Colts squad. Don't be surprised if he finally breaks the 100-yard rushing mark in this one. away.headline: Colts will take calculated risk, if Jonathan Taylor plays today
away.blurb: The NFL's injury report places no obligation on teams to disclose that a player will be a healthy scratch. The world finds out if a player who is able to play otherwise won't be playing roughly 90 minutes before kickoff, when the team supplies its list of inactive players. For the Colts, there's a decision to be made later this morning. Will running back Jonathan Taylor play at Jacksonville, as they continue to engage in talks aimed at trading him? (The Giants are definitely making a play to get him, and others presumably are, too.) By all indications, Taylor will play. But if the phone rings before 11:30 a.m. ET and the Colts get an offer they choose not to refuse, the plan could quickly change. (And since the Giants don't have a game this weekend, they can focus their efforts exclusively on trying to get it done, even if it takes a call from coach John Harbaugh to owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon.) Three weeks ago, the Cardinals knew on Friday that they'd be trading receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. after Sunday's game. Harrison didn't play. It's possible that one of the teams interested in Taylor will put the right terms on the table in order to persuade the Colts to put Taylor in bubble wrap for Sunday pending a post-game announcement that Taylor will be changing teams. Without a deal in place imminently, the Colts will be taking a calculated risk if Taylor is active. If he gets injured, the trade market will evaporate. Like it did on Friday for the Commanders and defensive tackle Daron Payne. There were trade talks regarding Payne, until he suffered a season-ending foot injury in practice. So even though the trade deadline doesn't arrive until November 10, there are various other deadlines that could drive a trade decision. For the Colts, the most immediate deadline arrives very soon, when they have to decide whether to let Taylor play and risk an injury that would necessarily close the door on a potential trade.

away.headline: Game rewind: Jacksonville Jaguars hammer Colts at EverBank Stadium
away.blurb: Jaguars-Colts report card gives out high marks for efficiency, defense The Jaguars have a short week and go back on the road for a Thursday night game on Nov. 5 at the Baltimore Ravens . The next three games will be on the road before the Jaguars return home on Nov. 29 vs. Tennessee. Because of the emphasis on running the ball out of multiple tight-end sets, the Jags' wide receivers had a quiet day. But Brian Thomas Jr., opened the scoring with a 12-yard TD reception, and as a group they all blocked well. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. The Chargers are coming off their bye week, though, so perhaps they can use that to their advantage this week. picks.blurb: Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Winners & Losers NBA Power Rankings 183 men's hoops games today Bears vs. Seahawks preview Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. Sources: The #hargers are signing former Ravens and Titans CB Jalyn Armour-Davis," NFL insider Jordan Schultz wrote on his official X account. "The former Alabama standout started 10 games for Tennessee last season before suffering a torn Achilles. He's now fully healthy and back in the NFL." "Chargers sign cornerback Jalyn Armour-Davis," NFL Wire Report wrote on its official X account on Monday. "Former Alabama standout returns from torn Achilles." Made NFL Leap after One Season as Starter The Ravens may have reached a bit by drafting Armour-Davis in the 4th round (No. 119 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft after just one season as a starter for Nick Saban at Alabama. In the Ravens' defense, Armour-Davis, 6-foot and 197 pounds, led his team with 3 interceptions in 2021, earning All-SEC honors, and later ran the 40-yard dash in 4.39 seconds at the NFL Scouting Combine. NFL draft analyst Lance Zierlein correctly predicted Armour-Davis would be a 3rd- or 4th-round pick. "One-year starter from a Nick Saban defense with prototypical traits but a lack of consistency in using them," Zierlein wrote in his 2021 pre-draft evaluation. "Armour-Davis is long, fast and talented, but is a developmental prospect, which is unusual for an Alabama cornerback entering the NFL. He should be unencumbered by scheme and possesses a profile that screams press-man. He's more linear than fluid and will give ground at break points, but he has the burst to make it up. If he can learn to play with his back to the football, the downfield completions will dry up quickly. He's a willing and reliable tackler in run support and could help on special teams early on. Improvement is likely with more experience, so a grade leaning more heavily to traits over tape appears to be necessary." Ravens Cut Bait on Armour-Davis After 3 Seasons The Ravens cut Armour-Davis as part of their final roster cuts in 2025 after 3 seasons of watching him battle one injury after another — including going on season-ending injured reserve twice in three seasons. Armour-Davis only played 4 games as a rookie before a hip injury ended his season. In 2024, he played in 7 games with two starts before he suffered a season-ending hamstring injury. Los Angeles Rams have no clear date for Myles Garrett's return McVay has yet to decide whether the Rams will open Garrett's 21-day practice window, which would allow the defensive end to begin working toward a return. Speaking to reporters on October 26, the coach said he needed to consult the team's medical staff before making that call. Early reports suggested he might return after four weeks, but the recovery period later stretched to six weeks or longer. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported last week that Garrett was likely to return to practice, with a possible Week 8 appearance in the discussion. Opening the practice window would not guarantee an immediate return to games. The Rams would have 21 days to activate Garrett to the 53-man roster or place him on season-ending injured reserve. Until the team makes that move, he cannot play. Other reports have suggested the wait could continue. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on October 21 that Garrett was likely to miss at least another two or three weeks. That timeline could push his return toward Week 10, with the Rams scheduled to have a bye in Week 11. Los Angeles improved to 3-4 after beating the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, but the team has little room for further setbacks. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. away.headline: Chiefs dealt double injury blow before facing Broncos
away.blurb: The Chiefs won the first meeting between the two teams in Week 1, demolishing the Broncos 31-10. But Denver has responded well since then, and now has the opportunity to move ahead of their division rivals in the standings. With the Broncos’ defense allowing just 18.3 points per game since Week 2, Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs’ offense will have their work cut out for them. Unfortunately, Kansas City’s defense now won’t have two of their best players. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has been downgraded to out with a shoulder injury after being listed as questionable on Friday’s injury report, while veteran corner L’Jarius Sneed has been placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Sneed will miss at least the next four games, leaving the Chiefs without two important members of their secondary against Denver. Sneed is also dealing with a recurring injury, with the knee issue forcing him to be limited in practice on Thursday and Friday. But his being placed on IR clearly signals the injury is more serious than anticipated, with Week 12 viewed as his expected return date. In six appearances this season, Sneed has recorded 32 combined tackles (22 solo), three pass breakups, two forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery. The Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos will meet for an important AFC West showdown on Sunday, with the division lead on the line. Kansas City enters at 5-1 after suffering their first loss of the NFL season in Seattle last weekend, while Denver is 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak after beating the Cardinals in Arizona. home.headline: Broncos injuries: Zach Allen and 3 others cleared to play
home.blurb: Allen went down in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals and appeared to be favoring his right hamstring. He was able to walk off the field into the team's blue medical tent, but did not return to the game. Allen finished the game standing on the sideline without his helmet as Denver closed out a win. After the game, Allen was asked about the injury and said, "Yeah, I'll be fine. Yeah, I'll be good." He was listed as questionable for today's game on Friday's injury report. Allen (and all of the players listed as questionable) are active and set to play against the Chiefs today. Denver Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen ( hamstring ) is active for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Allen has been one of the best interior defensive linemen in the NFL this season, totaling 24 tackles, 19 quarterback hits, 4.5 sacks, two pass breakups and one forced fumble through seven games. He's well on his way toward earning another first-team All-Pro nod after securing the first such honor of his career last season. The Broncos ' defensive line rotation this season has been led by Allen ( 343 snaps ), Malcolm Roach ( 283 ), Eyioma Uwazurike ( 272 ) and D.J. Jones ( 220 ). home.headline: Denver Broncos Injury Report Heading Into Week 8
home.blurb: Let's take a look at some of the injuries the Denver Broncos have dealt with throughout the 2026 NFL season, looking at both sides of the ball and who is out short- and long-term. Surtain suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 4 game against the 49ers and has been sidelined since. The All-Pro cornerback was a limited participant throughout Week 7 but returned to full participation this week. He carries no injury designation and is expected to return against Kansas City, which is a huge boost for the Broncos' defense. Hufanga, on the other hand, suffered his ankle injury during Denver's Week 5 victory over the Chargers and has missed the Broncos' last two games. He didn't practice this week and has been ruled out for Sunday's game. The Broncos have ruled out two players for Sunday's game and listed four others as questionable. Along with Hufanga, running back RJ Harvey has been ruled out after suffering a knee injury during the week. Harvey was added to the injury report Thursday as a limited participant but did not practice Friday. Defensive lineman Zach Allen, offensive tackle Garett Bolles, safety Brandon Jones and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle are all listed as questionable for Sunday's game. All four were limited participants Friday, and their availability will be determined closer to game day. We'll see if the Broncos can get back to full health for their huge divisional matchup against the Chiefs, but the biggest news for Denver this week is the return of Surtain, who immediately strengthens a Denver secondary that relies heavily on man-to-man coverage.
