With that in mind, I asked the following question this past week: What are your predictions, bold or otherwise, for the Miami Dolphins' defense and offense in this coming Sunday's game vs. the New England Patriots? Who do you expect to lead the team in key categories like tackles, tackles for loss, pass breakups, interceptions, defensive touchdowns, etc., on defense, and receiving yards, touchdowns, receptions, rushing production, and first downs, etc., on offense? What are your stat-line projections for our key playmakers this week, and/or who will be the team's MVPs on each side of the ball? Below are some of your takes and predictions for tomorrow's game- DalFinsFan is rightfully curious about this oddity in the schedule that seemingly helps a team from a colder climate that just happens to be the Pats. Curious why this is a late game instead of a 1:00pm ko. dedstrk says make it mistake-free and maybe? We need mistake free football and for the Pats to not take the Dolphins seriously enough for most of the game. Run the ball and continue on with the explosives and running the ball for first downs with Malik and OG. Phinette says the route to victory is keeping the ball out of the Pats' offense's hands. Our best shot at pulling off the upset is by controlling the clock. We need to stick with our ground game and avoid the costly three and outs. On defense we have to avoid being torched by the deep ball. If we can force the Pats to grind it out we have a shot. Phoenix6 has Miami narrowly edging out NE for victory #2. Defense: 1 sack, 1 fumble recovery, 2 interceptions. Rodriguez MVP. Offense: Ollie 89yds, 1 TD. Malik 289yds passing, 49yds rushing, 3 TDs. Douglas MVP. Dolphins 🐬 28, Patriots 27. coluccim believes that bad weather would be our best friend on Sunday. Our pass D is god awful, really. Pray for rain Phins1972 is much more focused on the rookies' development across the roster over the final score. We got our one win, and at this point I'm less concerned with the scoreboard than I am with seeing which players take a step forward and which ones don't. I really wish there were a young edge rusher on the roster who looked like a legitimate developmental piece. I'm still not a believer in Chop Robinson. He's played better lately, and credit where it's due, but I'm not sold yet. I'm interested to see whether Caleb Douglas can build on his recent performance and make an impact again. It would also be encouraging to see Chris Bell put together a solid outing. On the ground, I'd love to see Ollie top 100 yards once more. If Miami gets one of those hot, humid afternoons, a big back consistently moving the chains could have Patriots defenders gasping for air by the fourth quarter. If they can keep the game reasonably competitive, that'll be a positive. At this stage, player development is every bit as important as the final score, if not more so. Bill Hazlett has the defense doing their job well enough tomorrow to give us the W. Defense holds up. 28-17 Fins! JUK has Miami dropping this one by double digits. The Pats are clearly a stronger roster top to bottom. I think we will need to win the turnover battle to have a chance which has been the pats weakness but if Maye keep things clean they should win. It's likely to be a tough day for Willis if they get ahead too, as their secondary is so much stronger than our receiver room. We need to keep it close and run the ball well to have a chance. I'll say pats by 10 finfanfromsiam points to this team's long-standing issue covering any decent TEs. Does NE have TEs?? Nuff said…… CluelessNFLfan says that reality sets back in with another loss. The Phins come back down to earth this week. Pats 24, Phins 17. Robert Burstein has Miami losing by two TD's. I do think Miami can keep this game a little close until half time, but overall I think D.Maye will have a big game passing and making plays running. I've got Miami losing 13-27. Jptapt is being positive. Molly Polly II sees another upset on the horizon. I'm calling for an upset…why not! Patriots are favored +7.5. Defense tightens up shot group, Ollie beast mode another 100+ yards. Malik playing at home, confident, ready to prove he's the guy who can lead this team. Huge upset, Finz win with seconds left on the clock, 26-24! 🐬🐬 Gusman says it might be close, or Maye might just make the Dolphins' secondary look silly. If Drake Maye plays as he has for the past 4 games he should carve up the Dolphins secondary. Miami should be able to limit the Pats run game. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. Well, the vote is split, with some of us agreeing with Vegas that the Dolphins are clearly set up for another loss, while others are feeling a bit more positive after pulling out the win last weekend against the NY Jets. As always, I want to thank each of you who makes an effort to join our discussions and answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day. Please join us tomorrow for full game coverage and, of course, the live game thread.

away.headline: Patriots hit with double dose of bad injury news day before Dolphins game
away.blurb: The Patriots listed running back TreVeyon Henderson as questionable to play the Dolphins due to an illness on the final injury report on Friday. New England also listed wide receiver A.J. Brown as questionable to play due to knee and ankle injuries. Both players did not participate in practice on Thursday or Friday. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Patriots downgraded Brown and Henderson to out on Saturday. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks that kept him out until New England played the New York Jets in Week 6. On Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the knee injury Brown is dealing with this week is separate from the high-ankle sprain injury he suffered against Seattle. He wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday. “Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player,” Vrabel said , via the Patriots’ website. “He just wasn’t able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. So, we’ll continue to treat him, and then we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” The New England Patriots will be down two key offensive players when they travel to play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. More News: Exclusive: Breakout NFL Executives Who Could Become Future General Managers More News: 4 QBs Generating Serious Trade Buzz Weeks Before NFL Regular Season Starts Brown has nine receptions for 101 yards this season. New England traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for Brown in the offseason. Henderson has 203 yards rushing and one touchdown on 52 carries. The Patriots are 4-3 coming off a 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 7. Henderson had just nine yards on three carries against Chicago. Brown caught three passes for 88 yards. The Dolphins earned their first win of the season in Week 7 against the New York Jets. For more on the Patriots and the NFL , head to Newsweek Sports . away.headline: Patriots injury analysis: Pats get a much-needed reprieve in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7 | Pats Pulpit Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A New England Patriots Community Pats Pulpit November 2, 2026 Pats Pulpit Notifications Notifications Sections News Notifications New England Patriots Injuries Analyzing the Patriots’ injury situation before their upcoming game against the Dolphins. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. away.headline: Eagles missing Saquon Barkley, 2 starting WRs at Thursday's practice
away.blurb: The Philadelphia Inquirer's Zach Berman noted the limited depth, suggesting that another roster addition might have been expected if Barkley were in serious danger of missing Sunday's game. However, not making another move does not guarantee Barkley will be available against Washington. None of the three has been ruled out for Sunday, but their continued absence from practice makes Friday's final injury report especially important. The Philadelphia Eagles could be without several important offensive contributors for Sunday's matchup against the Washington Commanders , with running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks absent from the portion of Thursday's practice open to reporters. ESPN's Tim McManus and Olivia Reiner said all three players were missing as Philadelphia began its first full practice of the week after Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The absences are particularly concerning because the team listed all three players as nonparticipants on Wednesday's estimated injury report. Philadelphia held a walkthrough Wednesday, so the participation designations were projections rather than based on actual practice activity. Philadelphia Eagles Barkley continues to deal with hamstring and back injuries after leaving Monday's loss to Dallas. The veteran returned against the Cowboys after missing two games with a hamstring issue, but his back tightened during the contest, eventually forcing him to the sideline. His absence Thursday adds to uncertainty in an Eagles backfield already depleted by injuries. Philadelphia placed Dameon Pierce on injured reserve Wednesday, leaving Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue as the only other running backs on the active roster. Pierce emerged as a key contributor during Barkley's previous absence, leading the team's running backs with 151 offensive snaps over seven games. The Eagles promoted Blue from the practice squad Wednesday, but they haven't added another running back to the active roster. Philadelphia also continues to monitor Smith and Wicks, who missed Monday night's loss because of hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively. Their absences have put additional responsibility on rookie Makai Lemon, who caught his first career touchdown against Dallas, and the remaining members of the receiving corps. For Tanner McKee, losing multiple offensive playmakers would create another significant challenge as the Eagles try to end their five-game losing streak. Philadelphia enters Week 8 averaging just 18.1 points per game, ranking near the bottom of the NFL in scoring. Losing Barkley and two established receiving options would further limit an offense struggling to sustain drives. The Eagles' official Thursday injury report will provide more clarity on Barkley, Smith, and Wicks' participation levels. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Eagles-Commanders Final Injury Report: Saquon Barkley WILL play
home.blurb: Barkley returned to practice on Friday — albeit in a limited capacity — after being listed under did not participate on Wednesday and Thursday. There’s no question that Barkley wanting to play and help his team try to turn the season around is admirable. But the team should protect him from himself and sit him down if he’s not nearly healthy enough to play and remain in the game. Which is reasonable to think that’s the case considering he wasn’t even able to fully participate in a practice this week! While overcompensating for his hamstring injury, Barkley injured his back on his first rushing attempt in Week 7 and then played sparingly through obvious discomfort the rest of the game. What’s the point of that? What if he gets further injured? That’s not only a setback as it relates to this season, which very well might be cooked anyway, but potentially long-term as well. It could also prevent teams from making offers not only ahead of the NFL trade deadline but in the offseason, too. Even if you’re not of the mind he should be traded at any point, you should want him healthy for next year! I just think playing him is a short-sighted decision with much more downside than upside. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Jihaad Campbell, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smith and Wicks did not practice this week ahead of their second straight game missed; the Eagles will once again be without their top two wide receivers. With Covey also out, the Eagles only have four healthy wide-outs on the roster: Darius Cooper, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, and Elijah Moore. Against the Cowboys last week, Cooper played the most snaps of any Eagles WR while Lemon was right behind him. Despite this, Cooper only saw three targets while Lemon saw eight. The team will probably look to force-feed their rookie first-round pick again in this matchup. To be determined if they’ll look to elevate a fifth receiver from the practice squad. Bennett fully participated in practice all week. He’s still in his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve. away.headline: Is Jadarian Price playing against the Bears? Latest Seahawks RB injury update for 'Monday Night Football'
away.blurb: Week 8 concludes on Monday night in Seattle, as the Seahawks (4-3) host the Chicago Bears (5-2) at Lumen Field. Running back Zach Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in Seattle's NFC divisional round playoff win against the San Francisco 49ers in January, is primed to make his 2026 season debut. He doesn't have a game status on Seattle's final injury report, indicating he will be available to play. The situation for First-round rookie running back Jadarian Price is slightly murkier. Why the lack of clarity with Price's situation? That is because Price, who has missed the last four games with a chest injury while on injured reserve, would need to be activated by 4 p.m. today. Seattle, however, has already designated Price to return with ESPN among those reporting he will play. "We're going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one," coach Mike Macdonald said. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery. Those ranges are general medical guidance, not a diagnosis of Monangai. Four weeks and three missed games fit the Grade 2 range. That timeline is typical for an injury that required a specialist and a boot, while milder sprains resolve faster and higher-graded ones linger longer. Chicago has kept Monangai off IR, which requires a minimum four-game absence, because the team expected a shorter timeline.
